newsitem.title: EGYPT: Kurd leader says cooperation with Baghdad natural.
newsitem.headline: Kurd leader says cooperation with Baghdad natural.

text.p: Kurdish leader Massoud Barzani was quoted on Monday as saying that cooperation with Baghdad was the natural way to solve the Kurdish question, provided it accepts democracy and recognises a federal system for Iraq.

"The natural way (to solve the Kurdish issue) will be with the central government if it believes in such a solution on the basis of democracy, plurality... and recognition of federality," Barzani told the London-based Arabic daily al-Hayat.
Iraqi Kurds have been calling for a federal system linking the Kurdish north with the other parts of the country.

Barzani, leader of the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), defended resorting to Baghdad for military help, saying his forces would not have had the power to resist the alleged alliance between Iran and a rival Kurdish faction, the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) of Jalal Talabani.

"The Iranian military intervention to support the PUK was very large and very serious to the extent that it threatened our existence. Had we not asked for Iraqi military support, the balance of power would have been completely changed to the PUK/Iran side," he added.
PUK guerrillas were defeated in a 10-day drive through northern Iraq by KDP troops.
The KDP campaign began on August 31 with the taking of the Iraqi Kurdish capital Arbil with help of tanks-backed Baghdad troops, and ended last week with the seizure of Sulaimaniya.
